TimestampPrecision/v1 (proposed, requires C-001 acceptance): ASCII extended calendar timestamp YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.fraction](Z|+HH:MM|-HH:MM), using ASCII [0-9] digits only, with exactly 1..6 decimal fractional-second digits if present. Year/date must be a real Python-supported Gregorian date; local hours00..23 and minutes/seconds00..59, offset hours00..23 and offset minutes00..59 are checked lexically BEFORE datetime conversion. Offset seconds/fractions, naive timestamps, alternate separators/date forms and leap seconds are outside this contract. More than six fractional digits is TIMESTAMP_PRECISION even when extra digits are zeros; reject with source/record/line/column=timestamp before any parsing, rounding, truncation, duplicate comparison, day filtering or publication. Other lexical/range defects are addressed TIMESTAMP_FORMAT; invalid real dates or UTC normalization overflow are addressed TIMESTAMP_VALUE. Every accepted instant is represented exactly at integer-microsecond precision in aware UTC datetime; offset conversion uses whole minutes and must preserve the exact instant. No current owner approval or broader ISO8601 support is implied. Blank fields, bad UTF-8, malformed quoting and inconsistent widths reject. Whole source is validated before selecting a day.

contracts.semantics: UniqueMeasurements/v1: immutable ordered tuple of records(sensor_id:str,observed_at_utc:aware UTC datetime with an exact integer-microsecond instant,temp_c:finite binary64,addresses:immutable original source/record/line provenance). Canonical identity uses exact sensor_id plus the exact UTC microsecond instant; .000001 and .000002 are distinct events, equivalent offset representations of one accepted instant share identity. Unsupported submicrosecond input is rejected, never collapsed into a false duplicate/conflict. One record per canonical identity after complete CSV validation and duplicate conflict barrier, with no selected-day filtering. Runtime object shared directly in one process; no JSONL/database intermediate.
